paragraphs: July runs on your ruler. Mars spends the month in Gemini, your solar third house of errands, messages, and neighborhood logistics, and it opens loudly: Mars meets Uranus on July 4, which is the sky's version of a group chat catching fire. Expect the surprise text, the sudden plan, the detour that turns out to be the point. Say yes to the fast ones, but reread before you hit send.

The month's real weight sits at home. The Sun squares Saturn in your sign on July 6, and the friction is familiar: obligations to family or household pressing against what you're trying to become. The new moon in Cancer on July 14 is the reset that squares like that ask for, a genuine fresh start under your own roof, whether that's a lease, a conversation, or a room finally cleared. Mercury has been retrograde in the same territory all month; it stations direct on July 23, so let domestic negotiations and paperwork settle after that date rather than before.

Two stations land in Aries itself: Neptune turns retrograde on July 7, and Saturn follows on July 26. Both are slow-planet weather rather than daily news, but the Saturn one is worth respecting, the discipline project you started this spring goes into review mode through year's end. Keep what held; drop what was posture.

Then the sky pays for the effort. The Sun enters Leo and your fifth house of pleasure, romance, and self-made things on July 22, and meets Jupiter there on July 29, the brightest day on your calendar this month, made for the launch, the date, the opening night. That same day's full moon in Aquarius lights your house of friends and future plans: something you make for joy finds its audience. Mars sextile Saturn on July 19 already gave you the proof, speed and structure, for once, on the same side.

Money moves first this month. Mars and Uranus share Gemini, your solar second house of income and what you own, and they meet on July 4. That is the surprise expense, the sudden side offer, the subscription you cancel out of principle. Quick money decisions are fine through that weekend as long as they are reversible; the irreversible ones can wait.

Venus, your ruler, enters Virgo and your fifth house of romance and self-made pleasure on July 9, which sweetens the middle of the month considerably, the date, the studio afternoon, the thing you make because you want to. Just watch July 13, when Venus squares Uranus back in that money house: the impulse purchase will be wearing a very good disguise. Plan something inexpensive and excellent instead.

The new moon on July 14 lands in Cancer and your third house, errands, siblings, the neighborhood orbit. It is a real fresh start for a message, a course, a local commitment. Mercury has been retrograde in that same house all month, though, and it stations direct on July 23: draft the email and the agreement now, send and sign after the 23rd.

The finish is domestic, and bright. The Sun enters Leo and your fourth house of home and family on July 22, then meets Jupiter there on July 29, the best day of the month for the housewarming, the offer on the place, the family table with everyone actually at it. The same day's full moon at 6° Aquarius lights your tenth house of career, so something public peaks at the exact moment the home news arrives. If July 27's Sun-Pluto opposition puts a demanding voice from work on the line, you are allowed to let it ring. This round goes to the house.

For once the sky moves at your speed. Mars is in Gemini from the first of the month to the last, your solar first house, and on July 4 it meets Uranus, also in your sign. That is initiative with a live wire in it: the announcement, the haircut, the thing you finally quit. The next day, July 5, Mars trines Pluto and sextiles Neptune, which gives the bold move both traction and a reason. If you have been waiting for a starting gun, this is what one sounds like.

The money picture asks for more patience. Mercury, your ruler, is retrograde in Cancer, your second house of income, until it stations direct on July 23. The new moon there on July 14 is the right moment to pick the financial goal: the rate you will ask for, the budget you will actually keep. Set it on the 14th; sign it after the 23rd. The Sun's square to Saturn on July 6 sketches the tension early, a cost on one side, a commitment to friends or a long-range plan on the other. Only one gets funded this month, and that is fine.
July 19 is quietly useful: Mars in your sign sextiles Saturn in your eleventh house, and the people who share your long game show up with actual help. Take it.

Then the month hands you the microphone. The Sun enters Leo and your third house of messages, pitches, and the near neighborhood on July 22, and meets Jupiter there on July 29, the best talking day of your year. Send the pitch, publish the piece, make the ask you have been rehearsing. That same day's full moon in Aquarius falls in your ninth house of travel and study: the faraway thing, the trip, the application, the audience in another time zone, comes to a head at the exact moment you find the words.

Your year restarts on July 14. The new moon lands at 22° Cancer that morning, your solar first house, and it is the cleanest reset the calendar offers you. One caveat: Mercury is retrograde in your sign until July 23, so treat the weeks around the new moon as revision rather than debut. Rewrite the bio, rebook the appointment, repair the friendship. The launch keeps better after the 23rd.

July 6 is the day to keep your temper filed. The Sun in your sign squares Saturn in Aries, your tenth house of career, the deadline that ignores your birthday month, the boss who wants it anyway. Meet the obligation without renegotiating your whole job on the spot; Saturn stations retrograde on July 26, and the pressure that felt permanent goes into review through fall.

Mars spends the month in Gemini, your twelfth house, backstage. Its meeting with Uranus on July 4 can register as restlessness with no visible cause, or a sudden need to vanish for a day. That is not a crisis; it is a scheduling instruction. Book the actual rest. The quiet work pays anyway: Mars sextiles Saturn on July 19, and something finished privately earns credit publicly.

Then the ledger turns friendly. The Sun enters Leo and your second house of income on July 22 and meets Jupiter there on July 29, the single brightest money day of your year. Send the invoice. Have the raise conversation. Name the number without apologizing for it. The same day's full moon in Aquarius falls in your eighth house of shared finances, so a joint matter, the loan, the reimbursement, the split, comes to a head at the same time. Settle it on the 29th, while the light is good.

The first three weeks are the wind-up. The Sun sits in Cancer, your solar twelfth house of rest and the backstage, until July 22, and Mercury is retrograde there until July 23. The new moon on July 14 lands in that same quiet territory: use it to close the old year on purpose. Cancel what you kept out of politeness, sleep unreasonable amounts, let the drafts stay drafts. Your season is coming; arrive rested.

Your friends will not be resting. Mars and Uranus meet in Gemini, your eleventh house, on July 4, the invitation that materializes an hour before it happens, the plan that reroutes twice and improves both times. Say yes to the holiday-weekend chaos; that corner of your chart is where the month is loudest until yours begins.

Jupiter has been in Leo since June 30, and on July 20 it opposes Pluto in your seventh house of partnership: as your momentum becomes visible, someone close may respond by gripping tighter. The Sun repeats the opposition on July 27. Neither day calls for a showdown, just say where you are going, and mean the invitation to come along.

Then the sky clears its throat. The Sun enters your sign on July 22 and meets Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, the brightest day of your year, not just your month. Launch the thing, throw the party, make the ask that felt too big in March. And because the same day's full moon at 6° Aquarius falls in your partnership house, the answer arrives in person: a relationship reaches full clarity right as you reach full volume. The 29th is the whole point of your July. Build toward it.

Work gets loud before you do. Mars spends July in Gemini, your solar tenth house of career, and it collides with Uranus there on July 4: the reorg, the scope change, the client who discovers a deadline over the holiday weekend. You are the person who can fix it, which is exactly why you should decide out loud what fixing it costs. July 19, when Mars sextiles Saturn, is the day the dust settles into something durable, the approval, the signed-off plan.

Mercury, your ruler, complicates the social calendar: it is retrograde in Cancer, your eleventh house of friends and future plans, until July 23. The new moon there on July 14 genuinely does open a new circle or revive an old plan, just confirm every date twice and expect the group thread to contradict itself until the 23rd.

Venus enters your sign on July 9, which suits you: for the rest of the month you look the way you feel on your best days. When Venus squares Uranus on July 13, the temptation is to let a chaotic Monday at work talk you into reinventing yourself by Friday. Keep the haircut; skip the resignation letter.

The month ends in your favorite register, privately. The Sun enters Leo and your twelfth house on July 22, then meets Jupiter there on July 29: the best day of the month is one nobody else sees. The finished draft, the retreat, the long unscheduled afternoon. That same day's full moon at 6° Aquarius lands in your sixth house of workload and routine, so the sprint you have been running crests and clears at once. Finish it, hand it off, and take the quiet win with both hands.

The public part of your month comes first. The Sun crosses Cancer, your solar tenth house of career and reputation, until July 22, and the new moon there on July 14 is a genuine professional reset: the application, the title conversation, the portfolio finally reorganized. One timing note: Mercury is retrograde in that same house until July 23, so write everything on the 14th and submit it after the 23rd.

July 6 names the month's central tension. The Sun squares Saturn in Aries, your seventh house, the job pulling one way, the partnership pulling the other, both with a point. Saturn has been asking your closest relationship to grow up all year; it stations retrograde on July 26, and the agreements you made in spring go into review through fall. Reread them together rather than separately.

Two smaller weathers, worth using. Mars and Uranus meet in Gemini, your ninth house, on July 4, if a trip proposes itself out of nowhere, book it before the fare changes its mind. And Venus, your ruler, slips into Virgo and your twelfth house on July 9: schedule real solitude on purpose, because the social battery you pretend is infinite is not.

You will want it charged. The Sun enters Leo and your eleventh house of friends on July 22, then meets Jupiter there on July 29, the best social day of your year, the room where the introduction that matters actually happens. The same day's full moon at 6° Aquarius lights your fifth house of romance and creative work: something you love reaches full volume in front of exactly the right people. Go to the party on the 29th. Stay late.

Distance suits you this month. The July 14 new moon at 22° Cancer lands in your solar ninth house, travel, study, and what you actually believe. That's the fresh start: the course you enroll in, the trip you finally plan, the conviction you say out loud. One asterisk: Mercury is retrograde in the same territory until it stations direct on July 23, so sketch the itinerary early but buy the nonrefundable parts after that date. The Sun's square to Saturn on July 6 names the obstacle in advance, your workload, arguing that you can't possibly leave. It's arguing; it isn't right.

Mars spends July in Gemini, your eighth house of shared money and private arrangements, and the opening weekend is loud: Mars meets Uranus on July 4, the surprise statement, the joint-account jolt, the renegotiation nobody scheduled. The next day is better than it looks. Mars trines Pluto on July 5, your two rulers cooperating, which favors the deliberate money conversation over the reactive one. If something needs signing, the Mars sextile to Saturn on July 19 is the steady day for it.

Career is the big story late. Jupiter is newly settled in Leo, your tenth house, and the Sun joins it, entering Leo on July 22, then conjunct Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, the month's brightest professional day. Put the visible thing on it: the pitch, the review, the launch. Notice what pulls the other way, though. Jupiter opposes Pluto on July 20, the Sun repeats it on July 27, both dragging the same axis toward your fourth house of home, and the July 29 full moon lands at 6° Aquarius in that very house. On the day work applauds, something domestic comes to a head. Go home for dinner anyway.

The stations are quieter weather: Neptune turns retrograde on July 7 and Saturn on July 26, both in your sixth house of routines and health. The regimen you built this spring goes under review through year's end. Keep the parts you actually do.

Jupiter, your planet, is settling into Leo and your solar ninth house, travel, study, the far edge of the map, and July gives it a proper welcome. The Sun arrives in Leo on July 22 and meets Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29: the month's best day, and yours in particular. Book the trip around it, sit the exam near it, publish the thing on it. Jupiter's trine to Neptune on July 20 adds imagination to the planning, the destination that sounds slightly implausible is the one worth pricing.

Partnership supplies the plot twists. Mars is in Gemini, your seventh house, all month, and it meets Uranus on July 4, expect the person closest to you to do something genuinely unscripted. Give it room; the relationship is asking for movement, not an exit. Venus enters Virgo and your tenth house of career on July 9, and its square to Uranus on July 13 puts your work schedule and your partner's spontaneity briefly at odds. The durable version arrives on July 19, when Mars sextiles Saturn, a plan made together that actually holds.

Shared money asks for patience first. The Sun squares Saturn on July 6, an obligation involving someone else's resources pressing on your own commitments, and Mercury is retrograde in your eighth house until July 23, so joint paperwork signed before then tends to come back for edits. The new moon on July 14, at 22° Cancer in that same house, is the honest reset, the shared budget talked through, the application started clean. Just date the signatures after the 23rd.

One review notice: Saturn stations retrograde on July 26 in your fifth house, where Neptune has been retrograde since July 7, and a romantic or creative commitment from the spring goes into reconsideration through year's end. Meanwhile the July 29 full moon at 6° Aquarius fills your third house of messages on the month's brightest day, the phone will not stop. Answer the sibling first.

On July 6 the Sun squares Saturn, your planet, and the month states its theme early. The Sun sits in Cancer, your solar seventh house of partnership; Saturn sits in Aries, your fourth of home and family. Someone close wants more from you than the household currently has to spare, or the household wants more than the relationship does. Neither side is wrong. Set aside the week for it.

The repair kit arrives mid-month. The new moon on July 14, at 22° Cancer, is a clean start in that same partnership house, the honest conversation, the second chance, the contract renewed on better terms. Mercury has been retrograde there all month and stations direct on July 23, so give anything negotiated before that date one more read after it. Old agreements resurfacing in early July are material for the new moon, not verdicts.

Work runs hot and then sorts itself out. Mars conjunct Uranus on July 4, in your sixth house of routines, is the schedule flipped without notice, the outage, the coverage gap, the reorganized week. Mars sextile Saturn on July 19 is the fix that holds; lock the new routine in then.

Money is the late-month story, on both sides of the ledger. Jupiter opposes Pluto on July 20 across your eighth and second houses, what you share versus what is yours, and the Sun repeats the question on July 27. Then July 29 stacks the deck: the Sun meets Jupiter at 6° Leo in your eighth house, the month's brightest day, good for the loan approval, the settlement, the partner's good news, while the full moon at 6° Aquarius lands in your second. Send the invoice that morning.

Saturn itself stations retrograde on July 26 in your fourth house. The home project or family arrangement you committed to this spring goes into review through year's end, keep the load-bearing parts, renegotiate the rest.

For once, the month's closing act is addressed to you: the July 29 full moon lands at 6° Aquarius, your solar first house, and most of what comes before it is buildup. First-house culminations are personal. Something about how you live, look, or introduce yourself reaches full size, in front of witnesses.

The buildup runs through partnership. Jupiter is in Leo, your seventh house, and on July 20 it opposes Pluto in your own sign: a partner's expansion pressing on who you're becoming, the offer to merge homes, calendars, or plans, generous and a little engulfing at once. The Sun repeats the opposition on July 27, then meets Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, the month's warmest day, and that one belongs to the two of you. Make the offer, or accept it, and then, under your own full moon that same evening, check that the deal still fits the person you actually are. It probably does. Say so.

Romance and side projects get the early fireworks. Mars in Gemini, your fifth house, meets Uranus, your planet, on July 4: the spontaneous date, the idea that arrives sideways, the collaboration that starts as a joke. Mars trine Pluto the next day, July 5, gives it staying power. What sparks that weekend is allowed to become serious.

The unglamorous middle matters too. The Sun squares Saturn on July 6, your workload leaning on the errands-and-paperwork grind in your third house, and the new moon on July 14, at 22° Cancer in your sixth house, is the reset your routine has been asking for: the sleep schedule, the checkup, the calendar rebuilt around how you actually work. Mercury is retrograde in that same house until July 23, so book the appointments but expect the times to move until then. Saturn stations retrograde on July 26 in your third, the writing project or the sibling arrangement goes into review. A pause, not a cancellation.

Circle July 14. The new moon that day, at 22° Cancer, lands in your solar fifth house, romance, play, and the creative work that is yours alone. It's the cleanest fresh start of your summer: ask the person out, start the draft, book the studio time. The footnote is Mercury, retrograde in that same house until July 23, the old flame who resurfaces or the stalled project that stirs in early July deserves a look, but wait until after the 23rd to call it back on.

Partnership warms up on schedule. Venus enters Virgo, your seventh house, on July 9, and most of the month is easier for couples and close collaborators because of it. The one dated bump: Venus squares Uranus on July 13, when a household surprise tests everyone's patience, likely the aftershock of July 4, when Mars met Uranus in your fourth house and something at home changed without asking first. The appliance, the roommate's announcement, the sudden idea about moving. Gather the estimates early, but the Mars-Saturn sextile on July 19 is when the repair, the quote, or the family decision turns sensible.

Work grows, and pleasantly, if you pace it. Jupiter is in Leo, your sixth house of routines and health, and the Sun joins it, entering Leo on July 22, then conjunct Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, the brightest day of the month. Say yes to the bigger role that day. The caution is the axis it sits on: Jupiter opposed Pluto on July 20, the Sun repeats it on July 27, and both point at your twelfth house of rest, more work only holds up if the recovery is scheduled alongside it. Fittingly, the July 29 full moon at 6° Aquarius lands in that twelfth house the same day. Take the win, then take the night off.

About money: the Sun-Saturn square on July 6 prices the month's fun against the budget, and Saturn stations retrograde in your second house on July 26, with Neptune retrograde there since July 7. The spending plan goes under review through fall. Decide nothing dramatic, keep paying the same bills and let the numbers sit still.

August starts by asking what you are willing to take seriously because you enjoy it. Leo is your solar fifth house of pleasure, romance, and self-made work, and the Sun trines Saturn in Aries on August 7. That is not glamour. It is practice: the date that deserves planning, the creative thing that needs a schedule, the child or project that wants your steadier attention.

The middle of the month is even louder there. Mercury enters Leo on August 9 and runs straight into a stack of aspects on Wednesday, August 12: opposition Pluto, trine Neptune, sextile Uranus. That same day brings the new moon, a total solar eclipse, at 20° Leo. Keep the announcement simple; the audience, the dream, and the surprise variable are all in the room. Mercury meets Jupiter on August 15, and Venus sextiles Jupiter on August 17. If one day this month deserves the pitch, the invitation, or the opening night, choose the 15th through the 17th.

Partnership gets its own chapter once Venus enters Libra on August 6. The Venus trine to Pluto and opposition to Neptune on August 10 can make a relationship feel both fated and difficult to read. Ask the plain question. By August 21, when Venus opposes Saturn in your sign, the answer has to live inside time, limits, and actual behavior.

Home needs care, not drama. Mars enters Cancer on August 11 and squares Neptune on August 17, fogging the family conversation or household plan. Delay the righteous speech until you know what happened. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23, Mercury follows on August 25, and the August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse, at 4.9° Pisces lands in your twelfth house. Rest is not a moral failure. That same day, Mercury and the Sun both square Uranus: the calendar changes. Let it.

August begins at home. Leo is your solar fourth house, and the Sun trines Saturn on August 7 from that private territory to your twelfth house of rest. The message is not subtle: make the house quieter, make the boundary real, stop calling exhaustion a personality trait.

The real domestic reset arrives on Wednesday, August 12. Mercury, newly in Leo since August 9, opposes Pluto, trines Neptune, and sextiles Uranus that day, and the new moon, a total solar eclipse, lands at 20° Leo. A family conversation, lease matter, renovation, or room-by-room decision can move fast. Keep the plan flexible: Uranus is in Gemini, your second house, so the surprise probably has a cost. Mercury meets Jupiter in Leo on August 15, and that is the warmer day for the generous version, the family table, the good news, the big yes about where you live.

Venus, your planet, enters Libra on August 6 and your sixth house of work, health, and the small systems that keep a life running. Its trine to Pluto and opposition to Neptune on August 10 asks whether the routine serves your future or just looks graceful from the outside. The Venus-Jupiter sextile on August 17 helps; the Venus-Saturn opposition on August 21 insists the help needs structure.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your third house of messages and local motion. When Mars squares Neptune on August 17, do not answer the confusing text while angry. By August 23 the Sun enters Virgo, your fifth house, and Mercury follows on August 25. Pleasure returns, but the August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse, at 4.9° Pisces lights your eleventh house of friends just as Mercury and the Sun square Uranus. The group plan changes. The better one may be the second version.

August gives you the microphone, then asks you to use it carefully. Leo is your solar third house of messages, siblings, errands, and the near neighborhood. Mercury, your planet, enters Leo on August 9, and by Wednesday, August 12 it is opposite Pluto, trine Neptune, and sextile Uranus in Gemini. The sentence has reach. It also has consequences. Say the true thing, but do not make it harder than truth requires.

That same day, the new moon, a total solar eclipse, lands at 20° Leo. Start the writing project, local commitment, conversation, class, or pitch. Mercury meets Jupiter on August 15 in the same house, which is the month's best day for words that need to travel: the proposal, the announcement, the application, the message you want forwarded.

Money and workload ask for cleaner edges. Venus enters Libra on August 6, your fifth house, and August 10 can feel both magnetic and confusing as Venus trines Pluto and opposes Neptune. Enjoy the invitation without turning it into a life plan by midnight. Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your second house, then squares Neptune on August 17. A cost may be blurry, or a desire may be dressed up as necessity. Get the number in writing.

August 17 also brings Mercury trine Saturn and Venus sextile Jupiter, so the same day that muddles one corner steadies another. Choose the version with a receipt and a calendar. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23 and Mercury follows on August 25, moving attention to home and family. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse, at 4.9° Pisces lights your career house while Mercury and the Sun both square Uranus in your sign. A public matter peaks; your private life may not stay quiet while it does.

The month is blunt about money, value, and what you are willing to ask for. Leo is your solar second house, and the Sun trines Saturn on August 7 from there to your career house. A rate, role, invoice, or budget can get real because you treat it like a grown-up matter instead of a hope.

The middle of the month does more. Mercury enters Leo on August 9, then opposes Pluto, trines Neptune, and sextiles Uranus on Wednesday, August 12. That same day brings the new moon, a total solar eclipse, at 20° Leo. Start the new money plan, but make room for the hidden detail: taxes, shared resources, a friend's advice, or the private fear that has been steering the numbers. Mercury meets Jupiter on August 15, and Venus sextiles Jupiter on August 17. If you need to name the number, that window is the friendliest one.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, giving you more heat than usual. Useful, if aimed. On August 17 Mars squares Neptune in Aries, your tenth house, so do not let a vague professional pressure turn into a personal emergency. Ask what is actually due, by whom, and when. The answer may be smaller than the feeling.

Home softens once Venus enters Libra on August 6. Its trine to Pluto and opposition to Neptune on August 10 can make a family or household matter feel tender and overlarge at once. By August 21, when Venus opposes Saturn, the repair needs a boundary, not just goodwill. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23 and Mercury follows on August 25, shifting you into messages and local logistics. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse, at 4.9° Pisces lights your ninth house of travel, study, and belief while Mercury and the Sun square Uranus. The route changes; the larger direction does not have to.

This is your month, but not the loud kind. The Sun is in Leo until August 23, your solar first house, and it trines Saturn on August 7. That is a clean green light for serious self-definition: the promise you can keep, the plan you can repeat, the version of confidence that does not need applause to stand up.

The main reset arrives on Wednesday, August 12. The new moon, a total solar eclipse, lands at 20° Leo, and Mercury, newly in your sign since August 9, spends the same day opposite Pluto, trine Neptune, and sextile Uranus. You may hear yourself say something that changes the room. Good. Just remember Pluto is in your partnership house; the other person is not a prop in your reveal. Mercury meets Jupiter in Leo on August 15, your best day for the announcement, the ask, the introduction, or the first step into a larger role.

Venus enters Libra on August 6, sweetening your third house of messages and local plans. August 10 is more complicated: Venus trines Pluto and opposes Neptune, so a conversation can feel intimate and slightly unreal at once. Keep it beautiful, but check the facts. Venus sextile Jupiter on August 17 is easier; Venus opposition Saturn on August 21 asks whether the words match the commitment.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your twelfth house, and squares Neptune on August 17. Restlessness may have no obvious target. Do not invent one. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23, Mercury follows on August 25, and attention turns to money and self-worth. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse, at 4.9° Pisces lights shared resources while Mercury and the Sun square Uranus in your friendship house. Someone's plan changes the math. Recalculate before reacting.

The first three weeks are backstage. Leo is your solar twelfth house of rest, privacy, and unfinished business, and the Sun trines Saturn on August 7. That is useful solitude: the appointment kept, the old obligation closed, the quiet discipline that makes your next year possible.

Mercury, your planet, enters Leo on August 9 and makes August 12 unusually busy behind the curtain: opposition Pluto, trine Neptune, sextile Uranus. The same day brings the new moon, a total solar eclipse, at 20° Leo. Something private is ready for a reset, a sleep pattern, a secret worry, a draft, a goodbye. Do not rush to make it public. Mercury meets Jupiter on August 15, still in that hidden house, and the good news may arrive as relief rather than applause.

Money improves with manners once Venus enters Libra on August 6, your second house. Venus trines Pluto and opposes Neptune on August 10; the opportunity can be real, but the shared-cost piece may be foggy. Ask the extra question. Venus sextile Jupiter on August 17 helps you get paid for work done quietly, while Venus opposite Saturn on August 21 asks for a cleaner boundary around debt, obligation, or someone else's expectations.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your eleventh house of friends and future plans, then squares Neptune on August 17. A group promise may be badly defined. Put names next to tasks. Your season begins when the Sun enters Virgo on August 23; Mercury follows on August 25. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse, at 4.9° Pisces lands in your partnership house, while Mercury and the Sun square Uranus in your career house. A relationship reaches clarity just as work changes shape. Answer both, in that order.

Your month starts in the room where people know your name. Leo is your solar eleventh house of friends, collaborators, and future plans. The Sun trines Saturn on August 7, and a group plan can become real because someone finally agrees to the structure. Be that someone if nobody else volunteers.

Venus, your planet, enters Libra on August 6. That is a return of social ease, but not a free pass to blur yourself into everyone else's weather. August 10 is the test: Venus trines Pluto and opposes Neptune, pulling romance, friendship, and partnership into the same charged frame. If a bond feels enormous, give it a little time before you rename your life around it. Venus sextiles Jupiter on August 17, a much easier day for pleasure, introductions, and being liked by the right people. Venus opposes Saturn on August 21, and the same relationship has to show its practical side.

The new moon on Wednesday, August 12, a total solar eclipse, lands at 20° Leo in your eleventh house. Mercury entered Leo on August 9 and also opposes Pluto, trines Neptune, and sextiles Uranus that day. Start the shared project, but do not pretend everyone has the same motive. The motive does not need to be pure; it needs to be spoken.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your career house, then squares Neptune on August 17. A public obligation could become strangely slippery: unclear authority, vague instructions, a moving target. Get it in writing. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23 and Mercury follows on August 25, moving you toward rest. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse, at 4.9° Pisces lights your workload while Mercury and the Sun square Uranus. The schedule changes because it has to. Do less, better.

August is public. Leo is your solar tenth house of career, reputation, and the thing people can point to. The Sun trines Saturn on August 7, and the month rewards work with a spine: the portfolio cleaned up, the title clarified, the responsibility named instead of carried invisibly.

The career reset lands on Wednesday, August 12. Mercury has just entered Leo on August 9, and on the 12th it opposes Pluto in your fourth house, trines Neptune in your sixth, and sextiles Uranus in your eighth. The new moon, a total solar eclipse, arrives that same day at 20° Leo. A public beginning is possible, but it pulls on home, health, and shared resources at once. Do not call that a bad omen. Call it the full scope.

Mercury meets Jupiter in Leo on August 15, the best day for the pitch, interview, launch, or conversation with someone who can open a door. Venus sextiles Jupiter on August 17 from your private twelfth house, which suggests quiet support behind the scenes. Let the ally stay unnamed if that keeps the peace.

Venus returns to Libra on October 25, still retrograde, putting the work question back beside the relationship one. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 is yours: something you have been carrying personally reaches its visible end, and the Sun squares Pluto the same day. Let it finish.

Your ruler stations retrograde late in the month, so front-load anything that needs saying cleanly. October opens with Mercury square Pluto on October 2 (a conversation carrying more pressure than its subject deserves) and with Mars in Leo, your solar third house of talk, errands and the near neighbourhood, running three contacts in a week: trine Neptune on October 2, opposite Pluto on October 3, sextile Uranus at 5.4° on October 7. That last one is the good one. Uranus is retrograde in your own sign, and the sextile is the day an idea about yourself arrives usable rather than disruptive.

The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 opens your fifth house of pleasure, romance and the things you make for their own sake. It is the month's genuine beginning, and it wants play rather than output. The Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0° on October 15, linking that fifth house to Jupiter in Leo and your third: the pitch, the post, the sentence that carries further than expected. On October 16 Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your ninth house, and a long question about study, belief or somewhere you want to live stops circling.

Then the month narrows. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your sixth house of work and health; Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24 in the same house. Expect the schedule to argue with itself for a few weeks. That is not the week to add a commitment. Reread the last one instead. Venus re-enters Libra on October 25 while retrograde, warming the creative house again, and the full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 completes something private in your twelfth. Rest is the correct answer to that one.

Home is the month's centre of gravity. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 falls in your solar fourth house of home, family and where you are from. It is the cleanest reset of your year for the living situation, the room, the family arrangement. Before it, on October 4, the Sun opposes Saturn at 11.3°, that home angle against Saturn retrograde in your tenth house of work and public standing. It is the old argument between what the household needs and what the job takes. This year it is worth answering rather than postponing.

Mars spends October in Leo and your second house of money and what you own, which is unusually useful: trine Neptune on October 2, sextile Uranus on October 7, and trine Saturn at 10.4° on October 16. That last day is when earning and patience line up and a practical money move actually works. Mars opposes Pluto on October 3, across to your eighth house of shared and borrowed money, so early in the month one figure will feel like a power question. It is arithmetic. Treat it that way. Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius on October 16 in that same eighth house, and something contractual frozen since spring begins to move.

Venus is retrograde from October 3 at 8.5° Scorpio, in your fifth house: an old affection, an old creative project, or a child's situation coming back for another look. It returns to Libra and your home angle on October 25, still retrograde, which draws the two threads together. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and the fifth house warms; Mercury stations retrograde there at 21.0° on October 24. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 culminates in your eleventh house of friends and groups: one circle reaches its natural end or its clear commitment.

Mars is in your sign for the whole of October, and it does not sit still. It trines Neptune on October 2, opposes Pluto at 3.1° on October 3, sextiles Uranus at 5.4° on October 7, and trines Saturn at 10.4° on October 16. Read that as a sequence: imagination, then a collision with someone else's will in your solar seventh house of partnership, then a fast opening, then, best of the four, the day your drive and your patience finally agree. October 16 is the day to push something heavy uphill.

Jupiter is also in Leo, and on October 15 the Sun sextiles it at 22.0° from Libra and your third house of conversation and short trips. Say the thing. It travels further than you expect that week, and Jupiter in your own sign means the reception is warmer than the message strictly earns. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 resets that third house: a new rhythm of correspondence, a local arrangement, a sibling conversation restarted. The Sun opposed Saturn at 11.3° on October 4 before it, so the first week has the sharper tone: someone slows you down and you dislike it.

The second half moves indoors. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your fourth house of home, Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24 in the same place, and household logistics will need doing twice. Venus has been retrograde there since October 3, at 8.5° Scorpio, so the home question has been open all month; it moves to your third house on October 25, still retrograde. Then the full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 tops your tenth house of career, and something public completes. Pluto turned direct in your partnership house on October 16, and that is the quieter story underneath.

Money is the visible thread and health is the hidden one. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 opens your solar second house of income, possessions and what you are worth. It is the clearest financial restart of your year, and one worth making a plan around rather than a wish. It follows the Sun's opposition to Saturn at 11.3° on October 4, that money house against Saturn retrograde in your eighth: your resources against a shared obligation, stated plainly by someone else. Attend to the number, not the tone.

Your ruler has a complicated month. Mercury squares Pluto on October 2 and stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24, both in your third house of talk, errands and the local round. Between those dates, say the important things. After October 24, repeat them. Venus is retrograde from October 3 at 8.5° Scorpio in that same third house, which doubles the theme: old messages, old routes, an old neighbour or sibling thread reopening. Venus returns to Libra and your money house on October 25, still retrograde, so a price you agreed earlier comes back for review.

Two days carry the month's better weather. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0°, connecting your income to Jupiter in Leo and your twelfth house: help arrives from somewhere unadvertised, and you should accept it. On October 16 Mars in Leo trines Saturn at 10.4° while Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your sixth house of work and health: a body or work-shaped problem immovable since spring starts to shift, and you have the stamina that day to act on it. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 completes something in your ninth house: a course, a trip, a conviction reaching its end.

This is your season and it is not a simple one. The Sun is in your sign until October 23, and the new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 is your solar first house reset, the annual beginning that sets the tone for how you present yourself and what you start. Make it concrete. Before it, on October 4, the Sun opposes Saturn at 11.3° from your seventh house: a partner or close counterpart names a constraint, and October's work is deciding how much of it you accept.

Your ruler turns retrograde early. Venus stations at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3, in your second house of money and self-worth, and re-enters your own sign on October 25 still moving backwards. Read the whole month as a re-pricing: what you charge, what you accept, what you thought you were worth in August. The answer arrives slowly and should not be forced. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0°, linking your first house to Jupiter in Leo and your eleventh: friends and networks are the easy route this month, and one introduction is worth more than a fortnight of effort.

October 16 unsticks things. Mars trines Saturn at 10.4° and Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your fifth house, where a creative project or a romance frozen since spring starts to move again. Then the tone changes: the Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your money house, Mercury stations retrograde there at 21.0° on October 24, and financial admin gets slower and more careful. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 culminates in your eighth house of shared resources, and the Sun squares Pluto the same day. Something jointly held reaches its decision point. You will have the information by then.

Almost everything happens in your sign this month, and most of it moves backwards. Venus stations retrograde at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3, in your solar first house: six weeks of reconsidering how you look, what you want and who you want it from. Mercury squared Pluto from your sign on October 2 and stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24. The Sun arrives on October 23. So the last ten days put the Sun, a retrograde Mercury and your birthday season in the same place: loud, personal, and not the week for a final decision.

The first three weeks are quieter than that sounds. The Sun spends them in Libra and your twelfth house, which is the year's rest window whether or not you take it. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 is a private beginning: something started alone, unannounced, and better for it. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0° in your tenth house of career: a good word said about you in a room you are not in. On October 16 Mars in Leo trines Saturn at 10.4° and Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your fourth house of home and family, where a long-stuck domestic matter finally gives.

Two things then land together on October 26. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus culminates in your seventh house (a partnership reaches its visible peak or its honest end) and the Sun squares Pluto from your sign to that home angle. Between Venus retrograde in your first house and Mercury retrograde behind it, the instruction for the last week is narrow: gather the facts, say less than you want to, and let November decide. Venus leaves for Libra on October 25, which takes some of the heat out of it.

Your people are the month's best resource. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 falls in your solar eleventh house of friends, groups and shared projects. It is the cleanest reset of your year for who you spend time with and what you are building together. Ask for the introduction in the fortnight after it. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0°, and your ruler is in Leo and your ninth house of travel, study and conviction: the connection that opens a door somewhere further away than your current map.

Mars is in that ninth house all month and it is the engine. It trines Neptune on October 2, opposes Pluto on October 3 (a plan meets a flat refusal from your third house of everyday communication), sextiles Uranus at 5.4° on October 7, and trines Saturn at 10.4° on October 16. That last day is when the far plan becomes a booked, paid, scheduled thing rather than an intention. Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius the same day in your third house, and a conversation frozen since spring restarts.

The end of the month asks for quiet, which you will resist. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your twelfth house; Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24 in the same place. Old thoughts come back around, and most of them want reviewing rather than acting on. Venus has been retrograde there since October 3 at 8.5° Scorpio, so something unfinished and private has already been asking for attention. It moves to your eleventh house on October 25, still retrograde. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 completes something in your sixth house of work and health: a routine reaches the point where it either changes or stays for good.

Your career angle carries the Sun for three weeks and the year's clearest professional reset. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 opens your solar tenth house: a new role, a new title, or the same job restated on different terms. Start it deliberately. On October 4 the Sun opposed Saturn at 11.3°, your ruler retrograde in your fourth house of home, so the month's underlying tension is the honest one: what the work demands against what the household is owed. Saturn retrograde means the answer is a renegotiation, not a resignation.

Mars spends October in Leo and your eighth house of shared money, debt and other people's resources. It opposes Pluto on October 3 (one financial arrangement shows its teeth) and trines Saturn at 10.4° on October 16, which is the day to restructure rather than argue. Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius the same day in your second house of income, and money stuck since spring begins to move. Mid-month is where your leverage is: on October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0° in that eighth house, and someone with resources says yes.

Venus stationed retrograde at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3 in your eleventh house of friends and networks, so a professional friendship is under quiet review all month; it returns to your career house on October 25, still retrograde, which brings the review to the surface. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23, Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24, and group logistics get slower. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 culminates in your fifth house of pleasure and the things you make: a personal project reaches its finish, with the Sun square Pluto the same day. Take the finish.

Pluto is in your sign and October keeps knocking on it. Mercury squares Pluto at 3.1° on October 2, Mars opposes it on October 3, Venus squares it on October 20 and the Sun squares it on October 26: four contacts to the same degree of your solar first house in one month. The theme is consistent: other people press on who you are becoming, and the pressure is not personal even when it feels it. Between them, on October 16, Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius. That is the month's real event, and something in your own long remaking stops circling.

Mars is in Leo and your seventh house for the whole month, which is where the friction arrives from. The opposition on October 3 is the sharpest day; the sextile to Uranus at 5.4° on October 7 and the trine to Saturn at 10.4° on October 16 are the workable ones, when a partner's drive and yours point the same way. Jupiter is in that house too, and the Sun sextiles it at 22.0° on October 15 from your ninth house of travel and study: a partnership that opens a bigger horizon rather than closing one.

The Sun spends three weeks in Libra and that ninth house, and the new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 is the reset for it: the course, the trip, the argument you have decided to take seriously. Then the Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your tenth house of career, Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24, and public matters need double-checking for a few weeks. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 culminates at home, in your fourth house. Something about where you live reaches its answer.

October's money is other people's. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 falls in your solar eighth house of shared accounts, debts and what is inherited: a genuine restart for a joint arrangement, and the best fortnight of the year to renegotiate one. It follows the Sun's opposition to Saturn at 11.3° on October 4, that eighth house against Saturn retrograde in your second: someone else's terms against your own resources, said out loud. Neither side is unreasonable. Write the numbers down.

Venus stations retrograde at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3 in your ninth house of travel, study and belief, and Mercury stations retrograde there too, at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24. A plan to go somewhere, learn something or commit to a view gets reviewed twice over. That is not an obstruction; it is a chance to find the flaw while it is still cheap. The Sun enters Scorpio and that house on October 23, so the last week has the appetite even while the rest counsels patience.

Mars spends the month in Leo and your sixth house of work and health: opposite Pluto on October 3, sextile Uranus at 5.4° on October 7, trine Saturn at 10.4° on October 16. That trine is the month's most productive day for anything needing sustained effort. Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius the same day in your twelfth house, and something carried privately since spring starts to lift. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0° in your sixth: a practical offer of help at work. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 completes something in your third house: a conversation, a piece of writing, a local matter finishes.

Two reversals end a day apart this month, and most of November arranges itself around them. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in your solar eighth house of shared money and terms agreed to in a hurry. Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra on November 14, in the partnership house next door. Two adjacent rooms, both under review, both let go.

The approach is gentler than the arrival. Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7° on November 4, Libra to Leo, your seventh house in easy contact with your fifth, where pleasure and the things you make live. Then the new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 restarts the shared account four days before Mercury turns. The reset lands before the planet of terms moves, so this is the fortnight the joint money question gets loud rather than settled.

November 16 is the loud one. Mars, your ruler, meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo, both in your fifth house: appetite and scale at the same degree, pointed at whatever you do for the pleasure of doing it. On November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter at 26.1°, Scorpio against Leo, the eighth house asking the fifth what all this costs. Hear the question out before you answer it.

Then the month opens outward. The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and your ninth house of distance and study, and trines Neptune in your own sign at 1.7° on November 24, the same day the full moon at 2.3° Gemini fills your third house with every local, half written thing. November 25 is crowded: Sun sextile Pluto at 3.5°, Sun opposite Uranus at 3.7°, and Mars into Virgo and your sixth house, where the Leo blaze becomes a list. On November 30 the Sun trines Saturn at 8.0°, Saturn still in Aries. The question it has put to you all year, what you can actually sustain, gets asked gently for once.

Your ruling planet spends the first half of November still moving backwards. Venus stations direct on November 14 at 22.9° Libra, in your solar sixth house of work, health and the ordinary shape of a week, so the first fortnight is an approach, not a start. Venus sextiles Jupiter on November 4 at 24.7°, tying that work house to Jupiter in Leo and your fourth house of home: an easing between the job and the household.

The new moon on November 9 at 16.9° Scorpio lands in your seventh house, the one part of the chart that is not about you. Four days later Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in the same house. Two retrogrades ending within a day of each other, one in the house of the other person and one in the house of your working week: that pairing is the month. This is the fortnight the stalled conversation gets its words back.

November 16 is loud at home. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo in your fourth house, and on November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter from 26.1° Scorpio, so the household and the partnership pull against each other in one week. The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and your eighth house of shared money and debts.

Then both ends of the money question light up. The full moon on November 24 at 2.3° Gemini falls in your second house, your own earnings and what you actually value, and on November 25 the Sun opposes Uranus across that same axis at 3.7°. Mars enters Virgo the same day, which gives your hands somewhere easier to go. On November 29 Uranus trines Pluto at 3.5°, a slow agreement between what you earn and where you stand, and the Sun trines Saturn on November 30. The month ends steadier than it behaved.

The hinge of this month is two days wide and sits right in the middle. Before it, the month is mostly setup. Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7° on November 4, linking Venus in Libra, your solar fifth house of pleasure and the things you make, to Jupiter in Leo and your third, where you talk, write and run errands. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 opens the sixth: work, health, the shape of an ordinary day. It is a clean reset, arriving while the traffic is still stopped.

Then the hinge arrives. Mercury, your ruler, stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in that same sixth house, and the rereading ends. Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra the next day, November 14. Two retrogrades finishing on consecutive days is the month's real story: both planets stand still before they turn, and the handbrake comes off the work question and the creative one at once. The question they make loud is whether the revising is finished or has become the work.

Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo on November 16, both in the third house, Mercury's own territory and so familiar ground. That conjunction is loud wherever it falls, and here it falls on talk. On November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter at 26.1°, sixth house against third: the friction between how much you are saying and how much of the day is already spoken for.

The Sun enters Sagittarius and your seventh house of partnership on November 22, but the last week is mostly about you. The full moon at 2.3° Gemini on November 24 is in your own sign, with the Sun trine Neptune the same day: something about how you come across reaching its visible end, gently. On November 25 the Sun in Sagittarius opposes Uranus at 3.7° Gemini and asks it again, less gently, while Mars enters Virgo and your fourth house of home. Uranus trines Pluto on November 29. Whatever surfaced, let it stay up.

Two retrogrades end within a day of each other this month, and for you they end in the two rooms that matter most. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in your solar fifth house of romance, play and the things you make. Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra on November 14, in your fourth house of home and family. Everything before those two dates is the run-up.

The run-up is warm. Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7° on November 4, linking that home ground to Jupiter in Leo and your second house of earnings and what you value: the household and the money for it in easy contact. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 falls in the fifth house four days ahead of Mercury's turn in the same sign, which gives that creative start a second pass built into the timing. Begin anyway.

November 16 is the loud one. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo in your second house, appetite and opportunity in the same degree, and this is the week the money question gets loud. Two days later the Sun squares Jupiter at 26.1° on November 18, the fifth house against the second: what you are making, costed against what you are willing to spend on it. Say the number before the enthusiasm does.

The Sun enters Sagittarius and your sixth house of work, health and routine on November 22, and two days later the full moon at 2.3° Gemini lands in your twelfth, the unaccounted one. November 24 is a rest reckoning arriving exactly as the schedule tightens. Mars enters Virgo on November 25 and your third house of errands and plain speech sharpens. Venus sextiles Jupiter again on November 28, closing the loop it opened on November 4, and the Sun trines Saturn at 8.0° on November 30, the sixth house meeting the tenth. Nothing in November asks you to settle the whole thing. It asks what you are willing to keep making once the retrogrades stop handing you a reason to wait.

The large fact in your sky is Jupiter in Leo, which is your solar first house: your face, your appetite, the room you take up. Venus sextiles it from Libra on November 4 at 24.7°, out of the third house of talking and writing: a day when phrasing matters more than usual. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 is another register, fourth house, home and foundations, a beginning you make from underneath.

Then two planets turn around on consecutive days. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in that same domestic ground, and Venus does the same at 22.9° Libra on November 14, in the house of how you say things. Both had been retrograde: the rereading and the restating that goes with that stops, which is the month's largest event and its quietest. On November 16 Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo, both in the first house, a concentrated shot of personal fuel about as subtle as it sounds. On November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter from 26.1° Scorpio, home pulling against the version of you that just caught fire.

The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and the fifth house, familiar ground for a Leo: play, making things, performing because you like to. It trines Neptune at 1.7° on November 24 and the edges soften; the full moon that same day at 2.3° Gemini fills the eleventh house of friends. On November 25 the Sun opposes Uranus at 3.7°, setting what you make alone opposite the crowd it belongs to, and sextiles Pluto at 3.5° Aquarius, which puts a partner in the frame. Mars leaves your sign for Virgo the same day and the heat relocates to earning.

Venus sextiles Jupiter again on November 28 at 26.7°, the November 4 conversation without the retrograde, and Uranus trines Pluto at 3.5° on November 29. The Sun trines Saturn at 8.0° on November 30, fifth house to ninth: what you made for pleasure, set against what you actually believe. Worth asking what the fuel was for.

Two planets turn around a day apart this month, and the first is yours. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in your solar third house of talk, messages and the ordinary traffic of the mind. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 sits in the same house four days earlier, which puts a beginning and a reversal in one small room. Whatever you start writing or asking that first week is worth a second pass once your ruling planet turns.

Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra on November 14, in the house of your earnings and what you actually value. Two retrogrades ending that close together is the month's real shape: the sentence you have been trying to word and the number you have been avoiding come up in the same two days. Venus makes an easy angle to Jupiter on November 4 at 24.7° and repeats it on November 28 at 26.7°, Jupiter sitting in Leo and the private twelfth house behind your chart. Neither day asks loudly.

The middle of the month is loud where you cannot watch it. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo on November 16, both in that twelfth house: a lot of fuel burning in rest, old business, and the part of your life with no audience. The Sun squares Jupiter at 26.1° on November 18, your third house against that hidden one, and what you want to say rubs against what you are not ready to say.

The Sun enters Sagittarius and your home ground on November 22, and the full moon at 2.3° Gemini on November 24 lights your tenth house of work and public standing while the Sun sits at the base of the chart: house and career at opposite ends of one night. The Sun opposes Uranus at 3.7° on November 25, a degree and a half past where that moon stood. Mars enters Virgo the same day, out of the hidden house and into your own first. The Sun trines Saturn at 8.0° on November 30: a quiet, load-bearing end to a loud month.

Your ruler stops and turns around on November 14. Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra, in your own sign and your solar first house: the body, the face, the version of you other people meet before you have said anything. Weeks of that running in reverse end here. Ten days earlier, on November 4, retrograde Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7°, Jupiter in Leo and your eleventh house of friends and the long future, which is the easiest room on the chart that week.

The money half runs alongside it. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 lands in your second house, where your earnings and what you count as worth having are kept, and a day before Venus turns, on November 13, Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio in that same house. Two retrogrades ending within a day of each other is November's real story: the number and the self-image come out of review together.

Then it gets loud. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo on November 16, both in the eleventh, about as much collective heat as a year offers. On November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter from 26.1° Scorpio and the second house and the eleventh pull against each other. This is the week what the group wants and what you can afford stop agreeing. The figure is worth saying out loud.

The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and the month moves into your third house: talk, short trips, the people within a mile of you. The full moon at 2.3° Gemini on November 24 lights the ninth house opposite, and the Sun opposes Uranus there on November 25, so the near and the far argue. Mars enters Virgo and your twelfth the same day, where effort goes quiet. Venus sextiles Jupiter again on November 28, at 26.7° and moving forward now, the aspect the month opened with run the right way round. A good month to finish a sentence you started in October.

Two retrogrades end within a day of each other this month, Mercury on November 13 and Venus on November 14, and the first of them ends in your sign. Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7° on November 4 ahead of that, still retrograde in Libra and your solar twelfth house of rest and private matters. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 then lands in your first house, the one new moon all year that is simply about you.

Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, after three weeks of walking backwards through it. Venus follows at 22.9° Libra on November 14, so that retrograde ends out of sight, in the twelfth, after beginning in your own sign in early October. Most of the reconsidering happened in plain view. November 16 is the loud one: Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo in your tenth house of career. The Sun squares that Jupiter from 26.1° Scorpio on November 18, the week the gap between what you want and what the work wants is easiest to measure.

The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and your second house of income and worth takes over. On November 24 the full moon at 2.3° Gemini fills the eighth, the far end of that axis: joint accounts, debts, what is owed both ways. The Sun trines Neptune at 1.7° the same day, tying the money question to work and health in your sixth.

November 25 stacks three: the Sun sextiles Pluto at 3.5°, reaching your fourth house of home, opposes Uranus at 3.7° back across that money axis, and Mars leaves for Virgo and your eleventh house of friends. Venus repeats that sextile to Jupiter on November 28, forward this time. The Sun trines Saturn at 8.0° on November 30, income and daily work pointed the same way. Mercury's rereading ended on November 13. What the last week asks for is arithmetic.

The loudest aspect of November, Mars meeting Jupiter on November 16, lands before the Sun leaves Scorpio on November 22. Until then the Sun sits in Scorpio, your solar twelfth house, the quiet room before your own season, and the new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 starts something there with no audience attached. Venus sextiles Jupiter on November 4 at 24.7°, from your eleventh house of friends across to your ruler in the ninth, so the first week runs sociable and wide while the Sun is withdrawing. Company and the pull of somewhere further off get loud together, and the question is which one you are answering.

The real story is November 13 and 14. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio, then Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra: two retrogrades ending a day apart, one in the private house, one out among your people. Nothing resolves at a station. They stop going backwards, which is a smaller thing than it sounds and still enough to feel.

November 16 is the blaze. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo in your ninth house of distance, study and conviction, which is your own weather.
